subject: Post-demo model synthesis & vetting — shortlist + next steps
messages:
From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@latticehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — follow-ups from today

Vivek / Marissa,

Thanks again for taking the time today. The demo was helpful — I wanted to consolidate the things my team will need to evaluate model fit. High-level priorities we reiterated:

- P95 latency target: <= 250ms for 512-token requests (mostly summarization + guided extraction).
- Per-1k-token cost sensitivity: we need to keep model cost under a target budget (internal target: $0.18 / 1k tokens).
- Quality bar: accuracy on extraction prompts (we provide a labeled 500-case prompt set), and preservation of PII-handling rules.
- Compliance: HIPAA-friendly deployment options and audit logs.

Can you send a short recommended shortlist (2–4 candidate variants), quick rationale on cost/latency/quality tradeoffs, and any benchmark links or prompt sets we can run locally? Also would appreciate suggested next steps for a 2-week POC and what you recommend we can run as canary vs full rollout.

If possible, attach a lightweight prompt set and any perf CSVs so our infra lead can eyeball.

Thanks — I’ll loop in engineering on our side once we have the artifacts.

—Tom
Tom Nguyen
Director, AI Platform
Lattice Health
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@latticehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 19:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — follow-ups from today

Tom — thanks for the clear priorities, that helps a lot. Below is a concise synthesis + an action plan we recommend for a short POC. I’ve attached a sample prompt set (prompt-sets-v1.txt) and a CSV extract of the benchmark runs (bench-results-lattice-512-p95.csv). Links to the full benchmark dashboards are at the bottom.

Recommended shortlist (2–3 candidates) — with rationale at a glance:

1) rw-llama3-13b-int8 (default)
  - Quality: High for extraction + summarization on our labeled set (~94% extraction F1 in our run).
  - Latency: ~220ms p95 @ 512 tokens on g4dn-like instance with continuous batching.
  - Cost: Moderate (~$0.16 / 1k tokens in hosted config).
  - Tradeoffs: Best quality/latency balance; slightly larger memory footprint.

2) rw-llama3-7b-8bit-quant (quantized)
  - Quality: Slightly lower on edge-case extractions (~91% F1) but still within tolerable range.
  - Latency: ~160ms p95 @ 512 tokens on the same hardware.
  - Cost: Low (~$0.10 / 1k tokens).
  - Tradeoffs: Good if cost/latency are primary; monitor quality regressions on very long prompts.

3) rw-chronos-13b-slim (latency-optimized) — optional canary
  - Quality: Comparable on summarization, mixed on structured extraction (requires prompt tweaks).
  - Latency: ~120–140ms p95; ideal for user-facing low-latency paths.
  - Cost: Slightly higher than quantized 7b but lower than full 13b; complex ops can increase variance.
  - Tradeoffs: Use for latency-critical surfaces; may need tailored prompt engineering.

Quick notes on evaluation approach and quality regression monitoring:

- Baseline: Start by running your labeled 500-case set through the three candidates in parallel. We’ve attached the prompt set we used (prompt-sets-v1.txt) and the raw output CSV for our internal run.
- Thresholds: Define pass/fail thresholds during POC (e.g., extraction F1 >= 92% for production). If a variant crosses a soft regression (>= 3% drop vs baseline) we recommend automatic rollback.
- Canary plan: Begin with 5% traffic to the chosen candidate (rw-llama3-13b-int8 recommended), run live-eval against a holdout prompt stream and synthetic PII cases. Advance to 25% after 48–72 hours if no regressions.
- Auditing/compliance: Redwood Private options give you audit logs + KMS for keys; we can surface per-request logs to your SIEM with redaction rules for PII.

Next steps we suggest (week-by-week POC):

Week 0 (this week): Provide credentialed access to the eval harness + upload your labeled set (we’ll run parallel bench jobs).
Week 1: Run automated bench + live canary at 5% traffic. Tradeoff review call mid-week.
Week 2: Ramp to 25% if metrics stable; finalize canary playbook and design rollback triggers.

Action items from us (today):
- Share prompt-sets-v1.txt (attached) and bench CSV (attached).
- Grant temporary eval harness access: https://docs.redwood.ai/eval-harness/lattice-health (link below)
- Setup a 45-minute technical deep-dive for your infra team — propose Fri 21 May 10:00 PT or Mon 24 May 09:00 PT.

If you’d like, Marissa can provide a short cost-sensitivity chart for the first 6 months of expected traffic. Karthik will jump in on the technical deep-dive for kernel/runtime questions.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo model synthesis & vetting — shortlist + next steps

Tom — adding a few pragmatic operational points you might find helpful when you run the POC. These are things we use to reduce regressions during rollouts.

Operational safeguards we recommend (playbook highlights):

- Live-eval harness: run continuous scoring on a combination of your labeled 500-case set + a streaming holdout (we recommend 10k synthetic prompts to catch drift).
- Canary metrics to monitor: extraction F1, hallucination rate (false-positive structured fields), p95 latency, and per-request token cost.
- Regression triggers:
  * Soft: >= 3% drop in F1 OR p95 increase >= 30% => freeze rollout, increase sampling to 20% traffic to gather more data.
  * Hard: >= 6% drop in F1 OR new PII leakage event => automatic rollback to previous pinned model.
- Quantization caveat: when using int8/8-bit variants, watch very long sequences (>1k tokens) — KV cache patterns can lead to subtle accuracy regressions. Add a targeted long-sequence subset to the eval.
- Canary rollouts: we include an automated fallback routing policy (route to rw-llama3-13b-int8 if the latency SLO is breached on a request to the low-latency variant).

Attached is a short canary-run checklist and a one-page playbook (canary-rollout-playbook.pdf) — I’ll upload to the shared drive once you confirm.

If you want, I can prepare a short cost sensitivity table (monthly spend vs QPS and model mix) and send it before the deep-dive.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
